content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents the CenterFocus model for sovling the multi-person pose estimation and instance segmentation simultaneously. Specifically, it first uses a backbone to extract image features, then uses two heads for predicting keypoints and segmentation results. Then it uses two kinds of centroids, i.e., KeyCentroid and MaskCentroid to predict the 2D offsets, which are utlized to perform joint-level and pixel-level grouping. The evaluation are performed on several benchmarks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. The paper is well written

Weakness:
1. The centroid based offsets for grouping jonits and pixels is not new for human analysis, such as CenterNet and PersonLab. From this point, the contribution of this paper is very limited.
2. In addition, I think the comparison setting in experiments is not fair. For example in Table 2, for the comparison of pose estimation, the proposed approach actually utilizes segmentation results as auxiliary information, so the superior performance is not convincing.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper tries to propose a new method to combine keypoint estimation and instance segmentation tasks. Specifically, a KeyCentroid module and a MaskCentroid module are proposed.  The KeyCentroid module is designed to improve the accuracy of keypoint localization and the MaskCentroid module is proposed to integrate pixels into instance segmentation results.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
## Strength:
1. Strong experimental results. This paper shows better results on the COCO dataset and the OCHuman dataset.

## Weaknesses:
1. The contributions are incremental to the previous works.  The strong keypoints feature map, body heatmap, and Mask offset are much similar to the method in Ahmad et al. AAAI, 2022.  The difference between the proposed method and the previous methods needs to be clearly described.  

2. The dense vector prediction for keypoint localization has also been proposed by the previous paper, i.e. Single-Stage Multi-Person Pose Machines, ICCV, 2019.  

3. The submission claims that CENTERFOCUS is the first reliable application for the task of human pose estimation and instance segmentation. It is overclaimed as many previous methods have been proposed.

**4. Many paragraphs are similar to the previous paper, Ahmad et al., Joint Human Pose Estimation and Instance Segmentation with PosePlusSeg, AAAI, 2022.  I just list part of them below.**

(1) The section 'Instance Segmentation' in the related work in Ahmad et al. AAAI, 2022. 

>'There are two primary approaches for instance segmentation: (1) single-stage (Dai et al. 2016; Long, Shelhamer, and Darrell 2015; Bolya et al. 2019) and (2) multi-stage (He et al. 2017; Ren et al. 2015). The single-stage approach first create intermediate and dis- tributed feature maps based on the entire image, then assembles the extracted features for each instance to form the final mask. The InstanceFCN (Dai et al. 2016) uses fully convolutional networks to create several instance-sensitive scoring maps and applies the assembly module to the output instance. It requires repooling and other non-trivial computations (e.g., mask voting), making the real-time processing infeasible. YOLACT (Bolya et al. 2019) generates a set of prototype masks, then uses coefficient per instance mask to produce the instance-level segmentation.  '

The section 'Instance Segmentation' in the related work in this submission. 

>'There are two primary approaches for instance-level segmentation: (1)single-stage instance segmentation Dai et al. (2016); Long et al. (2015); Bolya et al. (2019) and (2)multi-stage instance segmentation He et al. (2017); Ren et al. (2015). The single-stage approachcreates intermediate and distributed feature maps based on the entire image. The InstanceFCNDai et al. (2016) create several instance-sensitive scoring maps and apply the assembly module tothe output instance. This approach is faster than the multi-stage approach; however, it requiresrepooling and other non-trivial computations (e.g., mask voting) that affect real-time processing.YOLACT Bolya et al. (2019) generate a set of prototype masks and then use coefficients per maskto produce the instance-level segmentation; however, it is critical to obtain a high resolution. '

(2)  The section 'Mask Offset' in Ahmad et al. AAAI, 2022. 

>'Mask Offset Human instance segmentation is a pixel-level classification challenge, i.e., how to connect pixels with the right instance I. We define the mask offset (MO) at each image position xi inside the segmentation mask of an annotated person instance j with 2-D mask pixel positions y_j,k where k = 1, ..., M, which point from image position xi to the position of the kth keypoint of the corresponding in- stance I_j. At each image position xi of a semantically identified human instance, the embedding vector e(xi) reflects our local approximation of the absolute location of each mask pixel of an individual to whom it corresponds, i.e., it represents the person’s expected shape structure. To this end, for each pixel, we learn the MO, illustrated in (Figure 5a), which points to the centroid (right shoulder). Here, we take advantage of the keypoint localization to use them as a center of attraction for each instance mask pixel. We also define the MO edge boundary to bound the MO pixel vectors in the embedding space. The purpose of the instance segmentation is to cluster a group of pixels P = {p0, p1, p2, ..., pi} and its 2-dimensional embedding vectors e(pi), into a set of in- stances I = {S0,S1,S2,...,Sj} to provide a shape along with pose. Pixels are assigned to their corresponding centroid: '

Section 3.3 MASKCENTROID in this submission. 

>'Human instance segmentation is a pixel-level classification challenge where to connect pixels with the right person instance I. For this task, we define MaskCentroid as illustrated in Figure 5 to cluster the mask pixels with the defined centroid Ci inside each annotated person instance with 2-D mask pixels, which points from image position xi to the position of Ci of the corresponding instance. At each image position xi of a semantically identified human instance, the embedding vector e(xi)reflects a local approximation of the absolute location of each mask pixel of an individual to whom it corresponds, i.e., it represents the person’s expected shape. To this end, for each pixel, we learn the pixel offset, which points toCi(right shoulder). Here, we take advantage of the high confident keypoint localization to use them as a center of attraction for each instance pixel. The purpose of instance segmentation is to cluster a set of pixelsP={m0,m1,m2,...,mi}and its 2-D embedding vectors e(mi), into a set of instancesI={n0,n1,n2,...,nj}to provide a 2D mask for the human instance. Pixels are assigned to their corresponding centroid:'

content.summary_of_the_paper: Overall, this paper proposes a bottom-up method to tackle the task of human pose estimation and instance segmentation at the same time. The proposed method is evaluated on COCO and OCHuman datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. I think it is interesting to solve the task of pose estimation and the task of instance segmentation at the same time.
2. The experimental results kind of demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Weaknesses: 
1. From my perspective, for a paper submitted to a certain conference, the template of the conference needs to be followed. However, this paper here and there does not follow the instruction of the conference. For example, most of the citation format in this submission does not follow the instruction of the conference (when to use \citep and when to use \citet).
2. Moreover, I think the writing skill of this paper may need to be improved. To be honest, this paper gave me a very hard time reading and I suspect the main reason is that in a lot of places, the authors only describe what they are designing but not why they are designing their method in this way. In other words, motivation is lacking.
3. With respect to the content, the main concern I have is what is the advantage of the proposed SKFM over the traditional heatmap-based pose estimation methods. Specifically, I kind of understand that the authors choose to regard pose estimation as a classification task. However, I am not sure why regarding pose estimation as a classification task is a better choice. In other words, this uncommon choice of regarding pose estimation as a classification task is not well-motivated.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: I believe that this paper is not presented in a clear way. Thus I am really not sure whether I can judge its novelty or not. Besides, as it seems this paper designed a somehow unique model architecture, I am also hesitating whether this paper produces enough details for reproducing their method.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, while this paper may have some interesting insight, the main concern I have for this paper in its current version is its presentation. Thus, after consideration, I tend to reject this paper.

content.title: CENTROID-BASED JOINT REPRESENTATION FOR HUMAN POSE ESTIMATION AND INSTANCE SEGMENTATION
content.abstract:
Joint pose estimation and instance segmentation combines keypoint heatmaps
with segmentation masks for multi-person pose and instance-level segmenta-
tion. Unlike easy cases with explicit heatmap activation, hard cases with im-
plicit heatmap due to multi-person entanglement, overlap, and occlusions requires
joint representation with a segmentation mask in end-to-end training. This pa-
per presents a new centroid-based joint representation method called CENTER-
FOCUS. It follows a bottom-up paradigm to generate Strong Keypoint Feature
Maps for both soft and hard keypoints and improve keypoints detection accuracy
as well as the confidence score by introducing KeyCentroids and a Body Heat
Map. CENTERFOCUS then uses the high-resolution representation of keypoint as
a center of attraction for the pixels in the embedding space to generate MaskCen-
troid to cluster the pixels to a particular human instance to whom it belongs, even
if 70% of the body is occluded. Finally, we propose a new PoseSeg algorithm
that collects the feature representation of a 2D human pose and segmentation for
the joint structure of the pose and instance segmentation. We then experimentally
demonstrate the effectiveness and generalization ability of our system on chal-
lenging scenarios such as occlusions, entangled limbs, and overlapping people.
The experimental results show the effectiveness of CENTERFOCUS outperforms
representative models on the challenging MS COCO and OCHuman benchmarks
in terms of both accuracy and runtime performance, Ablation experiments analyze
the impact of each component of the system. The code will be released publicly.
